log.summary: SBIFF 2027 Virtuosos (Coon, Navarrette, Jaafar Jackson, Eleazar, Ippolito +3) and Malkovich Outstanding Performer logged. DGA bars YCSE from feature directing (Fielder/Oppenheim −2).
Gold Derby odds move Fielder/Oppenheim into Best Director top five past Villeneuve (baselines adjusted). Sunrise on the Reaping first reactions glowing (Close +1). YCSE at $52M; DOC NYC Nov 11–19.
Chicago fest logged (closed Oct 25): Gold Hugo to The Dreamed Adventure; All of a Sudden screenplay; Club Kid, Elsinore audience. Savannah honors James Gray. NYFCC Dec 1, NBR Dec 2.
Montclair: Possible Love, Rehearsals for a Revolution win jury prizes; WHN, All of a Sudden audience awards. Palm Springs Vanguard to The Invite; SFFILM honors Artificial; PHM pushes Ortiz.
Coyote vs. Acme ruled eligible for Animated Feature (added, dark horse). IDA doc shortlists: six tracked docs incl. YCSE, Nuisance Bear. USC Scripter set for Feb 20.
Gotham noms logged: All of a Sudden, Clarissa, La Gradiva, Invite, TLC lead with 4; 67 nods recorded, 23 new contenders (Leigh, McKellen, Okonedo, Tatum, Closure). Winners Nov 30.
AFI Fest short Grand Jury Prizes (Oscar-qualifying) logged; A Woman's Place moved to Doc Short; Gotham tributes recorded; Odyssey acting slate set. Gotham noms still pending today.
Weekend actuals: YCSE $19.5M (+25%, $45.1M total); Wildwood $11.8M; Wicker solid $5.8M opening (Makeup +1). AFI Fest closed; prizes unreported. Gotham noms Oct 27.
Weekend box office: You Can See Everything projected ~$20M in wide expansion (No. 2); Wildwood soft ~$11M opening on $100M budget. AFI Fest ends today; Gotham noms Oct 27.
Oppenheim faces theft allegation over 2017 NYT short (YCSE, mild). Clayface (MC 59) and Wildwood (MC 85) open Oct 23. Zendaya to campaign lead for Dune 3 (untracked). Gotham noms Oct 27.
Middleburg audience awards: The Debut (narrative), La Bola Negra (intl), 14th (doc). Cinema Eye longlist: six tracked docs incl. YCSE, Naza. Feature noms Nov 12; Gotham noms Oct 27.
Added James Gray's Paper Tiger (NEON, Nov. 13; MC 77): Picture, Director, Driver and Johansson. No new festival or precursor results; London/Middleburg audience awards still pending.
No material changes. Middleburg and London audience awards still unreported; AFI Fest opens tonight (Oct 21–25); Gotham noms Oct 27.
You Can See Everything becomes Letterboxd's highest-rated film ever (buzz). AFI Fest underway with Behemoth!, Wild Horse Nine, Elsinore screenings. Middleburg/London audience awards still unreported.
No material changes. Middleburg audience awards still unreported; London audience awards due after Oct 21; AFI Fest opens Oct 21; Gotham noms Oct 27.
Heartland audience awards: I Play Rocky (shared), Elsinore, Tangles; Michael gets standing ovation at DGA FYC screening. Middleburg and London audience awards still pending.
No material changes (previous run completed earlier this morning; no new festival, precursor or Academy results confirmed).
YCSE opens to $15M (No. 2 doc opening ever); La Bola Negra record US per-screen avg; Sense solid, Whalefall soft; Woodstock doc prize to Rehearsals; Domingo Academy Museum honor.
YCSE pacing ~$12.5M, record doc opening; La Bola Negra now Spain's No. 4 film ever; London prizes logged; baselines updated to AwardsWatch October picks; Fielder/Oppenheim, Rogen added.
La Bola Negra opens in US (Metacritic 83) after topping €25M in Spain; Sense and Sensibility opens (MC 71); Once Upon a Time in Harlem MC 93. London and Middleburg prizes pending.
Hamptons (Oct. 13): La Bola Negra wins Best Narrative, Elsinore audience award, Pigeons Best Doc, Naza social justice prize, honors logged. YCSE hits Metacritic 98, $2M previews.
Busan: Majidi's Midday Meal wins Best Film (qualifies for Intl Feature, added); La Bola Negra audience prize. 14th AI backlash; Okamoto, Guitarricadelafuente up; Middleburg opens.
14th leads Critics Choice Doc noms (Naza, Harlem, Concrete, Rehearsals, YCSE also in); Elsinore wins Mill Valley narrative audience award. NYFF closed. Busan prizes Oct. 15.
Wildwood's London raves lift its Animated lead; Ray Gunn's mixed premiere dents it; Digger drops 60% in weekend two ($14.4M total). Busan prizes due Oct. 15.
Added the BFI London Film Festival (Oct. 7–18) to the Festivals tab with its galas. No new results or box-office moves since this morning; Busan prizes due Oct. 15.
No material changes since this morning's run; Busan prizes due Oct. 15, Middleburg opens Oct. 15.
The Social Reckoning bombed with a $5.5M opening (Picture, Adapted Screenplay and Jeremy Strong dip). No other material changes; Busan prizes due Oct. 15.
Artificial: Garfield moved to Supporting Actor and Borisov to lead per Neon's campaign; Metacritic 74 recorded; Variety's Oct. 8 Best Picture picks lift its odds onto the bubble.

Added the awards tracker: who won what at every festival and tribute so far (63 records). New: San Sebastián winners (Tender Loving Care's Golden Shell, La Bola Negra's audience award), TIFF and Telluride tributes, Busan, Robert Aramayo (I Swear, last season's BAFTA Best Actor) in Best Actor and Norway's Growth of the Soil in International Feature.
Site launched. Seeded all 24 categories (331 contenders, 108 films) from festival results Sundance through NYFF, AwardsWatch's September predictions, Variety's Oct. 1 tracking and October box office.

rules.text: Non-English films that win the Golden Bear (Berlin), Best Film (Busan), Palme d'Or (Cannes), the World Cinema Grand Jury Prize (Sundance), the Platform Prize (Toronto) or the Golden Lion (Venice) qualify alongside country submissions. The film itself is credited as the winner.

rules.text: A performer can now earn separate nominations in the same acting category for different films, as directors already could.
rules.title: Actors can be nominated twice in one category

rules.text: Writing nominees must be human-authored, and acting nominees must be billed performers whose roles were performed by humans with their consent.
rules.title: Human authorship and performance
